description: OptimizedMatcher vs ReferenceMatcher, same scenarios and build type as baseline.json (Module 8), for an apples-to-apples comparison.
notes: Both binaries built under the same no-CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE (debug-equivalent) config as baseline.json -- see environment.md's caveat that absolute numbers don't transfer to -O2/-O3.

Speedup is modest (~2%) on this debug build: OptimizedMatcher's win is fewer per-order heap allocations (vector append + tombstone vs. a std::list node per order), which a debug build's lack of inlining/allocator-fastpath optimization partly masks. cv_percent stayed under 1% across 5 repetitions on both sides, so the gap is real, not noise.

OptimizedMatcher trades memory for speed: canceled/filled orders are tombstoned (quantity=0) in place rather than erased, so a price level's backing vector never shrinks. Not exercised here since steady_limit_flow/burst_crossing are cancel-light; see the 2-line comment atop optimized_matcher.cpp.
10k-op ReferenceVsOptimized and FuzzMatcherParity tests (tests/parity/, tests/fuzz/) found zero trade/snapshot mismatches before these numbers were recorded.
